description: A single-panel scatter plot (no sub-panels) of microhardness HU in N/mm² versus prior heat treatment for (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals. The ordinate spans 1700 to 2250 N/mm² with horizontal dashed gridlines every 50 N/mm²; no numbers are printed at the data points, so values can only be located against the gridlines. The abscissa carries twelve rotated condition labels: as grown, 1100°C FC RT, 1100°C FC600°CQ, 250°C/14d, 300°C/6h, 300°C/3d, 300°C/14d, 320°C/233d, 400°C/6h, 600°C/6h, Q*, Q*+300°C/14d. Every point is a filled circle with a vertical error bar. Six conditions (as grown, 1100°C FC RT, 1100°C FC600°CQ, 250°C/14d, 300°C/6h, 300°C/3d) scatter tightly about the 2000 gridline. Longer or higher-temperature anneals lie lower: 300°C/14d is the lowest point (near the 1875 gridline), with 320°C/233d and 600°C/6h also below 1950 and 400°C/6h just below 1950. The two quench-related conditions, Q* and Q*+300°C/14d, are the highest, both plotted above the 2050 gridline. The figure demonstrates that heat treatment shifts HU by only about 5–10% around 2000 N/mm², the largest hardening coming from quenching from 1100 °C.

subfigures.description: Scatter/error-bar plot of microhardness HU (N/mm², ordinate 1700–2250 with 50 N/mm² dashed gridlines) against twelve heat-treatment condition labels on the rotated abscissa for (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals; each condition plotted as one filled circle with a vertical error bar. Values cluster near 2000 N/mm² except the long/high-temperature anneals (lowest, 300°C/14d, near 1875) and the two quenched conditions Q* and Q*+300°C/14d (highest, above 2050).

observations.observation: The figure is a single scatter plot with vertical error bars; the ordinate is microhardness HU in N/mm², labelled from 1700 to 2250 with dashed gridlines every 50 N/mm².

Twelve heat-treatment conditions are plotted on the abscissa in the order: as grown, 1100°C FC RT, 1100°C FC600°CQ, 250°C/14d, 300°C/6h, 300°C/3d, 300°C/14d, 320°C/233d, 400°C/6h, 600°C/6h, Q*, Q*+300°C/14d.
No numeric values are printed at any data point; hardness can only be read relative to the 50 N/mm² gridlines.
The highest two points are Q* and Q*+300°C/14d, both plotted above the 2050 N/mm² gridline, with Q* the higher of the two.
The lowest point is 300°C/14d, lying near the 1875 N/mm² gridline, well below the cluster of the other conditions.
The conditions as grown, 1100°C FC RT, 1100°C FC600°CQ, 250°C/14d, 300°C/6h and 300°C/3d all lie close to the 2000 N/mm² gridline and their error bars overlap.
320°C/233d, 400°C/6h and 600°C/6h plot below 1950 N/mm², i.e. below the main cluster but clearly above 300°C/14d.

The caption defines the condition abbreviations: 1100 °C FC RT = furnace cooling from 1100 °C to room temperature; 1100 °C FC600°CQ = furnace cooling from 1100 °C down to 600 °C with subsequent water quench; Q = water quench from 1100 °C.
The caption states the material is (111) oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals measured at room temperature.
The citing text states the observed hardness varies only by about 10% at most, i.e. does not depend sensitively on heat treatment.
The citing text states the highest hardness is shown by the specimen quenched from 1100 °C to room temperature (Q*), consistent with the topmost point of the plot.
The citing text states the hardness of the quenched specimen is only slightly reduced by the subsequent anneal at 300 °C, matching the small drop from Q* to Q*+300°C/14d in the plot.

The citing text concludes that short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness, since maximum-order (250 °C/14 day) and minimum-order (quench from 600 °C) states fall in the same cluster as the as-grown crystal.
Error-bar sizes differ between conditions, the largest extending roughly over one gridline interval (about ±50–60 N/mm²) for the quenched and low-hardness conditions.

unreadable_items: No numeric hardness values are printed beside the data points; all values are read only by position against the 50 N/mm² gridlines.
Individual error-bar magnitudes are not annotated and cannot be quantified exactly.
The asterisk/accent marks used in the axis labels Q* and Q*+300°C/14d are only partially legible at the supplied resolution.
